pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Language School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Language School.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Language School.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Language School.

2. When practising Pre Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Pre Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pre Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Pre Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.

3. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. going
   C. goes
   D. goed

4. When practising Phonics, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Phonics.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Phonics.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Phonics.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.

5. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. run
   C. happiness
   D. blue

6. When practising Language Welcome and, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Language Welcome and.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Language Welcome and.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Language Welcome and.

7. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. No full stops

8. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.

9. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.

10. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a describing word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

11. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.

12. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Word Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Connected text and fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Pre-Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.

3. A — went

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.

5. B — run

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.

7. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

10. D — A person, place, thing, or idea

11. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

12. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Word Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Connected text and fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Comprehension; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pre-Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
